CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypogonadism follow-up; gynecomastia evaluation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
64-year-old HIV-positive male presenting for follow-up of hypogonadism on testosterone replacement therapy. Patient reports feeling well with improved vigor and sleep quality since starting therapy approximately 5 months ago. Notes significant improvements in laboratory values, particularly triglyceride reduction from 265 mg/dL to 145 mg/dL and increase in red blood cell count which has remained stable. Patient is impressed with these improvements and notes the cardioprotective potential of improved triglyceride levels.

Patient is on testosterone 1 mL IM every 10 days delivering 140 mg. He maintains a medication calendar to track his injections and is currently on day 8 of his cycle, with next dose due Thursday or Friday. Patient asked about increasing his testosterone dose to 175 mg; however, physician counseled against this. Discussed that peak testosterone levels are already exceeding 1,500 ng/dL, putting him at higher risk for polycythemia and blood viscosity issues that could necessitate therapy discontinuation. Risk would astronomically increase with further dose escalation. Patient understood the rationale and agrees with current dosing.

Also takes finasteride 2.5 mg daily (half of 5 mg tablet) and Cialis 5 mg on workout days and 2.5 mg on other days, though currently out of Cialis. Patient inquired about indole-3-carbinol for estrogen control; physician noted that estradiol was not elevated on prior testing and is adequate. Offered to recheck in fall if desired. PSA remains stable at 0.6 ng/mL.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies weight loss. Reports good energy and sleep. No acute complaints. States he is taking correct steps to improve his life.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- HIV infection
- Hypogonadism
- Hyperlipidemia (improved)
- Gynecomastia

MEDICATIONS
- Testosterone: 1 mL IM every 10 days (140 mg)
- Finasteride: 2.5 mg daily
- Cialis: 5 mg on workout days; 2.5 mg on other days (currently out of supply)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works out regularly. Motivated to make positive life changes and improve his health. Uses Walmart pharmacy; prefers paper prescriptions.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Trim appearance
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no concerns on auscultation
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no concerns

RESULTS
PSA: 0.6 ng/mL (previously 0.5 ng/mL one year ago; normal <4 ng/mL)
Testosterone: Peak levels >1,500 ng/dL
Triglycerides: 145 mg/dL (improved from 265 mg/dL)
Red blood cell count: Elevated and stable
Estradiol: Not elevated on prior testing

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
64-year-old HIV-positive male with hypogonadism on testosterone replacement therapy.

1. Testosterone: Continue 1 mL (140 mg) IM every 10 days. Do not increase to 175 mg at this time. Discussed risks of dose escalation including polycythemia and increased blood viscosity given already elevated peak testosterone levels. Patient counseled regarding potential for therapy discontinuation if complications develop. Patient agrees with current dosing.

2. Finasteride: Continue 2.5 mg daily.

3. Cialis: Continue as tolerated (5 mg on workout days, 2.5 mg on other days). Refill prescription needed.

4. Estrogen control: Estradiol currently not elevated. No indication for supplemental estrogen-lowering agents at this time. May recheck estradiol in fall if patient desires.

5. PSA: Stable at 0.6 ng/mL. Continue annual monitoring.

6. Gynecomastia: Discussed today; will continue to monitor.

7. Lipids: Significant improvement in triglycerides and cholesterol noted. Continue current regimen.

8. Prescriptions: Refill testosterone, finasteride, and Cialis. Patient prefers paper prescriptions.

9. Follow-up: As needed.
